docs.title: 🧠 Smart Money Concepts (SMC) Masterclass: The Unlimited Depth Guide to Fair Value Gaps (FVG)
docs.text: Welcome to the most comprehensive, institutional-grade masterclass on Fair Value Gaps (FVGs). If you want to stop trading like retail and start seeing the market matrix exactly how algorithmic institutional computers (IPDA - Interbank Price Delivery Algorithm) see it, this is your blueprint.

docs.title: 1. The Core Philosophy: What is an FVG in algorithmic terms?
docs.text:
When retail traders look at a chart, they see support and resistance lines, trendlines, and candlestick patterns. Institutions do not see patterns; they see liquidity and imbalances.

A Fair Value Gap (FVG), also known as an Imbalance or Inefficiency, is a specific price range where a massive amount of liquidity was injected into the market in a single direction (either aggressive buying or aggressive selling). Because this price movement happened so rapidly, the market did not get a chance to offer the counter-party (the buyers during a sell-off, or the sellers during a rally) a "fair" chance to trade.

In simple terms: Price "jumped" over a specific level due to immense volume, leaving a void.

docs.title: Why do FVGs matter?
docs.text: The market algorithm is designed to achieve equilibrium. An FVG represents disequilibrium. Think of it like a vacuum in space—the market structurally must return to that void eventually to offer fair value to both buyers and sellers. We use these vacuums as our high-probability entry targets.

docs.title: 2. The Anatomy of an FVG
docs.text: An FVG is strictly a 3-candle formation. It does not exist with 2 candles, and looking beyond 3 candles will confuse you.

docs.title: Bullish FVG (BISI - Buyside Imbalance Sellside Inefficiency)
docs.text:
A Bullish FVG occurs during an explosive upward move. - Candle 1: A bullish candle (starts the move). We care about its High. - Candle 2: A massive institutional bullish displacement candle. This is the candle that breaks structure and creates the gap. - Candle 3: A bullish or bearish candle. We care about its Low.

The Gap: If the Low of Candle 3 does NOT touch or overlap with the High of Candle 1, the empty space between them on Candle 2's body is your Bullish FVG.

docs.title: Bearish FVG (SIBI - Sellside Imbalance Buyside Inefficiency)
docs.text:
A Bearish FVG occurs during an explosive downward move. - Candle 1: A bearish candle. We care about its Low. - Candle 2: A massive institutional bearish displacement candle. - Candle 3: A bullish or bearish candle. We care about its High.

The Gap: If the High of Candle 3 does NOT touch or overlap with the Low of Candle 1, the empty space between them is your Bearish FVG.

docs.title: Why does the market return to the FVG?
docs.text:
Imagine a central bank needs to buy 10,000 lots of EUR/USD. They can't just click "buy" because the market doesn't have 10,000 lots of sellers available at the current price. If they buy all at once, they will cause a massive price spike (generating Candle 2).

Because they caused this spike, many of their orders were triggered at unfavorable, higher prices. The algorithm then ceases aggressive buying, allowing retail traders to naturally push the price back down. Once the price returns to the "gap" where the original buying started, the institution activates the rest of their pending orders to accumulate more positions at a wholesale (discount) price.

This is why an FVG acts as a magnet for price, and then a trampoline.

docs.title: 4. How to Qualify a "High-Probability" FVG
docs.text: Not all FVGs are created equal. Out of 100 FVGs on a chart, only 5 are actually high probability institutional entry points. How do we filter them?

docs.title: Premium vs. Discount (The Matrix)
docs.text: You should NEVER buy a Bullish FVG if it is in a "Premium" (expensive) market pricing. You should NEVER sell a Bearish FVG if it is in a "Discount" (cheap) market pricing. 1. Take your Fibonacci Retracement tool. 2. Draw it from the absolute swing low to the absolute swing high of the current impulse move. 3. The 50% level is the Equilibrium. 4. Rule: Only buy Bullish FVGs that are below the 50% line (Discount). Only sell Bearish FVGs that are above the 50% line (Premium).

docs.title: Confluence with Order Blocks
docs.text: An FVG becomes incredibly powerful when it aligns perfectly with the top or bottom of an Institutional Order Block. An Order Block is the last down-candle before an explosive up-move (or vice-versa). If the FVG sits exactly at the threshold of this Order block, it is practically an automated sniper entry.

docs.title: Time of Day (Killzones)
docs.text: Institutions do not inject billions of dollars during dead market hours. High-probability FVGs are typically formed, and mitigated (tested), during specific algorithmic windows: - London Session: 2:00 AM - 5:00 AM EST - New York Session: 8:30 AM - 11:00 AM EST (Premium manipulation hours)

docs.title: 5. The "Unlimited Depth" Trading Strategy
docs.text: Here is a mechanical, step-by-step strategy to trade FVGs with zero emotion.

docs.title: Step 1: Market Structure Shift (MSS)
docs.text: Wait for the market to take out a significant structural high or low. This is the algorithm sweeping retail stop losses. Immediately after the sweep, the market MUST reverse violently, breaking a counter-structure level.

docs.title: Step 2: Displacement and Imbalance
docs.text: The violent reversal MUST occur with displacement. Displacement means the candles are huge, aggressive, and close near their highs/lows. This displacement move MUST leave behind a Fair Value Gap (FVG).

docs.title: Step 3: Patient Limit Orders
docs.text: Identify the FVG. - Place a Limit Entry Order exactly at the start of the FVG (the High of Candle 1 for a Bearish SIBI, or the Low of Candle 1 for a Bullish BISI). - Stop Loss: Needs to be placed completely outside the FVG, ideally above the body of Candle 1 (or the origin swing high/low). - Take Profit (Target): The algorithm seeks liquidity. Your target should always be the next major opposing swing high/low where retail stop-losses are resting. (E.g., if you are buying an FVG, target the previous "Double Top" or prominent High).

docs.title: Concluding Wisdom
docs.text:
Trading SMC using FVGs requires immense patience. You are no longer chasing breakouts. You are waiting for the algorithm to show its hand (Displacement), waiting for the trap to be set, and entering precisely where the algorithm returns to rebalance its books.

Mastering the FVG is mastering the literal footprints of smart money.
